class.name: NetwDisplayHistory
class.brief_description: One display channel's recorded samples and the total resample over them.
class.description:
A channel is one value stream smoothed independently of its siblings. [method record] keys each arriving value by tick, and [method sample] answers what the channel shows at a playhead placed anywhere in that tick space, including before the first sample and past the newest one. [codeblock] history (one channel), keyed by tick: 9 12 15 18 21 newest received = 21 |---- playhead ---| prev = 15 dt = 16.4 next = 18
displayed = sample(16, 0.4, ...) lerp(state[15], state[18], 0.4) [/codeblock] Two things pin on the first [method record] and hold for the channel's life. The tick domain, so a stream keyed by authoring ticks can never be mixed with one keyed by receive ticks, and the value type, so the sample loop never re-decides what it is interpolating. [method clear] frees the domain, because a teleported channel may legitimately be refed from the other one. [member sleeping], [method has_projected], [method get_project_age] and [method has_snapped] are what the last [method sample] decided. [DisplayCore] reads them into its per frame stats rather than deciding again.

method.name: bracketing_ticks
method.description: Returns the [code](prev, next)[/code] recorded ticks bracketing [param tick], each [code]-1[/code] when no such tick exists.

method.name: clear
method.description: Drops every recorded sample, wakes the channel, and frees the tick domain so the next [method record] may pin a different one. The value type survives, because a teleport does not change what the channel carries.

method.name: get_at
method.description: Returns the value recorded exactly at [param tick], or [code]null[/code] when nothing was. This is how a channel reads a sibling's derivative at its own newest tick, an atomic pair, so a torn pair never manufactures a phantom trajectory.

method.name: get_buffer
method.description: Returns the ring buffer holding the recorded samples, which [method NetwDisplayHandle.get_buffer] publishes for inspection.

method.name: get_project_age
method.description: Ticks past the newest sample the last [method sample] projected, already clamped to the forecast budget it was given.

method.name: has_projected
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the last [method sample] extrapolated past the newest recorded tick rather than reading between two of them.

method.name: has_snapped
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the last [method sample] or [method smooth_toward] took the [member snap_distance] escape instead of interpolating.

method.name: has_tick_after
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when a sample was recorded strictly after [param tick]. A playhead with nothing after it is starving, which is what grows the display lag.

method.name: is_empty
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when nothing has been recorded. An empty channel is never written, so the pump defers to whatever last wrote the property rather than clobbering it.

method.name: newest_tick
method.description: Returns the highest recorded tick, or [code]-1[/code] when the channel is empty.

method.name: record
method.description: Records [param value] at [param tick] and wakes the channel. [param authoring_tick] declares which tick domain [param tick] belongs to, and mixing the two on one channel fails rather than interleaving. A value equal to the one recorded last is dropped, so a stream that keeps resending a settled value neither grows the buffer nor revives a sleeping channel.

method.name: sample
method.description: Returns what the channel shows at [param dt] plus [param factor]. Before the first recorded tick the channel has no stream to show and [param last_written] holds. Between two recorded ticks the value is their interpolation, unless the bracket is farther apart than [member snap_distance], which jumps to the newer sample instead. A bracket wider than twice [param expected_interval_ticks] is a hole rather than a slow channel, so the older sample holds and only the last interval is spent crossing. Past the newest recorded tick the channel holds that sample, and sets [member sleeping] once the display already shows it. A [param forecast] playhead projects the tail instead, by [param explicit_velocity] when [param has_explicit_velocity] is set and by the finite difference of the last two samples otherwise, over an age clamped to [param max_forecast_ticks] and scaled by [param ticktime]. A velocity too small to move the display forfeits the projection and holds. A quaternion walks the arc whichever mode its channel declares, because the engine's own lerp already dispatches a quaternion to the spherical walk.

method.name: pass_verdict
method.description: What one display pass may do with this channel, one of [enum Pass]. [constant PASS_SKIP_SLEEPING] and [constant PASS_SKIP_EMPTY] both mean the channel is not written this pass, and they are distinct because only sleeping is a state worth counting: an empty channel has never been fed, where a sleeping one has caught up. Sleeping is answered first for that reason. [constant PASS_SAMPLE_PROJECT] is [param forecast] granted, and [param spec] can refuse it: a [constant NetwInterpolate.TAIL_HOLD] channel never projects however hard the entity forecasts. A channel with no [param spec] at all takes the default and may.

method.name: smooth_toward
method.description: Returns [param last_written] blended [param weight] of the way toward [param result], which is the exponential smoothing layered on top of a bracketed sample. A [param weight] at or above one takes [param result] whole, and a distance past [member snap_distance] takes it whole as well.

members.member: The interpolation algorithm, one of [enum NetwInterpolate.Mode]. It also decides how a difference between two values is measured, so an angle channel wraps rather than sweeping the long way.

[code]true[/code] once the channel has nothing left to show: its newest sample is already displayed and no later one has arrived. A sleeping channel is not written, so another writer may take the property over. Recording a distinct value wakes it.
Distance past which a move jumps instead of interpolating. [code]0.0[/code] disables it.

constants.constant: The channel has caught up and is not written, which leaves the property free for another writer.
The channel has no stream to show at all, so the pass defers to whatever wrote the property instead of clobbering it with a stale value.
The channel is sampled between its recorded ticks.
The channel is sampled and may project past its newest sample.
